plan: Model the component as a single CheckInConsole class holding a defensively copied appointment list, an id-to-label lookup, and the public `session` dict with exactly the four contract keys.

Centralize state transitions in `handle`, dispatching on `action["type"]` to one private handler per action type; each handler fully validates before mutating, so rejected actions can never leave partial state behind.

Express every rejection through a single `_error(text)` helper that builds a screen whose first message begins `Error:`, guaranteeing malformed input (non-dict actions, unknown types, wrong field types, unknown ids) never raises and never touches `session`.

Derive prompts from session state with a `_next_prompt` helper (unmet contact -> `Confirm contact`, unmet appointment -> `Choose appointment`, else `Review and complete`) so accepted contact/correction screens and error screens share one source of truth.

Build all screens through one `_screen(prompt, messages)` constructor that attaches freshly copied appointment choices exactly when the prompt is `Choose appointment` and an empty list otherwise, keeping the screen shape and choice ordering deterministic.

Implement `run_once` to check both injected collaborators up front (raising RuntimeError before calling either), then read one action, handle it, display the resulting screen exactly once, and return that same object — making the source and sink trivially replaceable by unittest fakes with `read_action`/`display` methods.
mechanisms: Validate-then-commit handlers: each action handler performs all checks before any assignment to `session`, preserving accepted data on failure.
Single screen factory `_screen` enforcing the exact prompt/messages/choices shape and the choices-only-on-`Choose appointment` invariant.
State-derived `_next_prompt` used for post-correction and error screens, so prompts always reflect the next unmet requirement.
Uniform `_error` path producing `Error:`-prefixed messages without exceptions for every invalid or malformed action.
Constructor-injected `action_source`/`screen_sink` duck-typed collaborators (`read_action()` / `display(screen)`) enabling standard-library unittest fakes.
Defensive copying of the appointment sequence at construction and of choice dicts at screen build time, preventing external mutation of internal or emitted data.
